title: Identification of Potent Cell Penetrating, Nontoxic Peptides for Inhibiting MDM2-p53 Interactions: Characterization of Anticancer Peptides via Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
authors: Pant, Pradeep; Sehgal, Aman; Gupta, Tushar; Sharma, Pradeep
journal: Journal of peptide science : an official publication of the European Peptide Society
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子动力学模拟筛选抑制MDM2-p53蛋白互作的穿膜肽，对象为蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，方法虽含MD但与本课题TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: Inhibiting MDM2-p53 interactions is a crucial therapeutic strategy in cancer treatment, as it can restore the tumor suppressor activity of p53 and inhibit tumor progression. Peptide inhibitors have shown promise in targeting this interaction; however, their optimization for in vivo use often encounters challenges, particularly in cellular uptake. The present study addresses this limitation by identifying cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) that are predicted to be nontoxic to humans and capable of inhibiting the MDM2-p53 interaction. We utilized a comprehensive CPP database to extract unmodified peptides, focusing on those predicted to be nontoxic. Selected candidates were subjected to molecular docking followed by 500-ns all-atom explicit-solvent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, performed in triplicates, to evaluate their binding stability and affinity with MDM2. Binding affinity calculations using MM-PBSA, AREA AFFINITY, and PRODIGY revealed that two peptides consistently exhibited stable binding to MDM2 and demonstrated higher affinity compared with the p53 reference fragment. These peptides not only maintained favorable interactions throughout the simulations but also showed strong potential to disrupt MDM2-p53 binding and reactivate p53 function. The findings highlight these peptides as promising nontoxic anticancer agents and provide a strong foundation for the development of peptide-based therapeutics targeting the MDM2-p53 interaction.
abstract_zh: 抑制MDM2-p53相互作用是癌症治疗中的关键治疗策略，因为它可以恢复p53的肿瘤抑制活性并抑制肿瘤进展。肽抑制剂在靶向该相互作用方面显示出潜力；然而，其体内应用的优化常面临挑战，尤其是在细胞摄取方面。本研究通过识别预测对人体无毒且能够抑制MDM2-p53相互作用的细胞穿透肽 (cell-penetrating peptides, CPPs) 来解决这一局限性。我们利用一个全面的CPP数据库提取未修饰肽，重点关注那些预测无毒的肽。选定的候选肽经过分子对接 (molecular docking)，随后进行三次重复的500纳秒全原子显式溶剂分子动力学 (molecular dynamics, MD) 模拟，以评估其与MDM2的结合稳定性和亲和力。使用MM-PBSA、AREA AFFINITY和PRODIGY进行的结合亲和力计算显示，两种肽始终表现出与MDM2的稳定结合，并且与p53参考片段相比具有更高的亲和力。这些肽不仅在模拟过程中维持了有利的相互作用，还显示出破坏MDM2-p53结合并重新激活p53功能的强大潜力。研究结果突显了这些肽作为有前景的无毒抗癌剂，并为开发靶向MDM2-p53相互作用的基于肽的治疗药物提供了坚实基础。
